public_rationale: The evidence establishes a narrow example of disappointed expectations, but does not settle the broader claim. METR's developers expected faster work and instead worked more slowly in early 2025. Its follow-up cautions against carrying that result forward unchanged. The broad firm survey reports small past effects alongside larger future expectations, which is not a missed forecast for the same period. Goldman Sachs explicitly placed the measurable macroeconomic effect later. These records neither establish nor rule out widespread disappointment by the post.
limitations: The speaker leaves the relevant population, productivity measure and expected timing unspecified.
Small experiments and retrospective executive reports cannot by themselves establish a broad expectations shortfall.
The ongoing observation is assessed through the latest complete quarter before publication.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: So far, AI has had less impact on real-world productivity than many people expected.

statement.excerpt: Coming soon: more on why AI has had less impact on real-world productivity so far than many people had anticipated.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that realized workplace productivity gains had disappointed expectations held by a substantial group. 'Many' need not mean a majority.
The comparison must concern gains previously expected by the observation period. Expectations for later years cannot establish disappointment by June 6, 2026.
Productivity means useful output relative to labor or other inputs. Adoption, investment, benchmark performance and employment changes alone do not measure it.
Read 'so far' cumulatively through the latest complete quarter before publication, ending March 31, 2026. Leave the start unspecified because Marcus supplies none.

A representative survey comparing earlier expectations with realized gains, or sufficiently broad matched studies, could establish the claim. One small occupational experiment establishes only a narrower example.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence shows that a substantial group previously expected greater AI productivity gains by the observation period than actually materialized. Expected and realized gains must concern comparable dates, populations, measures and adoption conditions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad evidence matching earlier expectations to realized AI productivity gains for the same period shows that expectations were generally met or exceeded and provides evidence against a substantial disappointed group. Positive gains alone do not contradict the claim.

evidence.locator: Opening paragraph; Methodology and Core Result sections provide sample and expectation details
evidence.explanation: Sixteen experienced open-source developers expected AI to shorten their work by 24%, but the experiment found longer completion times. This is a matched shortfall in one real workplace setting, not evidence establishing the breadth of Marcus's claim.

METR judged that developers likely benefited more by early 2026, while emphasizing selection problems and weak evidence about the size of the improvement. This limits extrapolation from e1 but does not establish whether earlier expectations were met.

evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning 'More than 90 percent of executives'
evidence.explanation: This research-publisher summary describes surveys conducted from November 2025 through January 2026: 89% reported no labor-productivity impact over the preceding three years. Its larger expected gains concern the following three years, so that comparison cannot establish missed expectations for the past.

evidence.locator: Section 'AI’s effects on GDP will take time to emerge', second paragraph
evidence.explanation: This prominent forecaster expected the measurable US macroeconomic effect to begin in 2027 and described productivity gains as dependent on widespread adoption over ten years. Modest gains before June 2026 therefore do not demonstrate disappointment against this forecast.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative survey or broad set of studies documenting what a substantial group expected AI to deliver by early 2026, compared with realized productivity for the same people or firms, dates, measures and adoption conditions.
